cases.question: When a SQLite WAL checkpoint encounters active readers or unavailable locks, how do PASSIVE versus FULL modes differ, and what test checks checkpoint lock release?
cases.scope: WAL checkpoint implementation and lock-related tests

anchors: releases all locks before returning a busy error.

rubric.fact: PASSIVE checkpoint avoids invoking the busy handler and may make only partial progress when read-locks are unavailable
An unavailable writer lock in a stronger checkpoint mode can cause a fallback to PASSIVE without promoting it to guaranteed completion
The WAL locking tests cover behavior after checkpoint lock contention and subsequent operations

cases.question: When SQLite replays a hot rollback journal after a crash, what does it do when a journal header or page record is malformed, and where is this tested?

anchors: Hot journal rollback related test cases.
journal-record for which the checksum fails.

rubric.fact: Malformed journal data stops playback at the corruption boundary instead of treating later bytes as valid records
The journal is handled differently for data corruption versus I/O or allocation failure, which returns an error and avoids deleting the journal
pager1.4 hot-journal tests cover invalid headers and checksum errors

cases.question: How does SQLite separate B-tree commit phase one from phase two, what does each hand off to the pager, and what is special about cleanup after a multi-file commit?
cases.scope: B-tree transaction commit implementation and pager handoff

rubric.fact: Phase one flushes prepared database changes through sqlite3PagerCommitPhaseOne, with optional super-journal coordination
Phase two finalizes the rollback journal and transaction state; the journal action commits the transaction
Multi-file bCleanup allows transaction state cleanup even after a pager phase-two error because the super-journal deletion already committed the transaction

policies.baseline: Git grep over exact checked-out commit; ranked by same question terms with explicit source-excerpt and cost receipt
policies.excession: excession agent locate using the identical question and 12-result limit; preserve reading_plan, coverage, cache/index costs
policies.outcome: Human-reviewed claim correctness with exact cited source support; retrieval-path coverage is only a proxy, never the outcome
policies.pairing: Same agent model, prompt, commit, tool privileges, budget; randomized arm order and isolated context per arm
policies.scoring: Rubric item correct only after reviewer checks explanation and source citation. Missing and unsupported claims remain visible.
policies.failure: No outcome score unless actual blinded agent responses and independent reviewer decisions are supplied
